area: schema — backend/schema.py, backend/lib/, backend/migrations/, and the webapp table list
summary: `backend/schema.py` is the single DDL authority for the pipeline's Postgres database. `ensure_schema(conn)` first refuses to run if `public.events` exists (the guard against being pointed at the other application's database, schema.py:461-466), then `CREATE TABLE IF NOT EXISTS` for fourteen tables and `CREATE OR REPLACE VIEW jobs_app`, all idempotent and called at the top of essentially every entrypoint (every ingest script, extract.py, match.py, score.py, cohort.py, searchqueries.py, api/query_claims.py, webapp/schema_web.py). Column additions that post-date a table are routed through `lib.dbconn.add_missing_columns`, which reads `information_schema.columns` first so the steady state issues no DDL and takes no ACCESS EXCLUSIVE lock (dbconn.py:149-175); this is where columns land without a migration on `jobs`, `job_facts`, `job_scores`, `job_events` and `job_ingest_state`. The three-tier cost model is real in the keys: `job_facts` is `PRIMARY KEY (job_id)` — one extraction per posting, shared by every profile — while `job_matches` and `job_scores` are both `PRIMARY KEY (job_id, profile)` (schema.py:545, 582, 514). `jobs_app` (schema.py:1148-1205) is the only supported read surface: it INNER JOINs `job_matches` (so a posting with no match row is invisible), LEFT JOINs facts and scores, and requires `status='open'` plus four non-empty completeness predicates that are deliberately not NOT NULL constraints. Staleness is per-table: score.py's `_STALE_ANY` (score.py:384-387) compares only `facts_version` (against the JOINED facts row, not the constant), `persona_sha` and `prompt_version`; `criteria_version` on `job_scores` is provenance only and a test pins that (tests/test_score_versions.py:277-296). On `job_matches`, by contrast, `criteria_version` IS a cache key (match.py:594). `lib/` is owned outright, not vendored — `lib/__init__.py:29-58` says it *was* shared as `pipelib` until 2026-07-26 and names the two in-repo drift guards. `lib/upsert.py`'s `UpsertResult.__iter__` yields exactly three values and omits `.errors`, which is the documented landmine that `upsert_checked` exists to close. The ten scripts in `backend/migrations/` are manual one-shots — dry-run by default, `--apply` to write, each documenting its own idempotency — and nothing in `run-daily.py`'s STEPS invokes any of them.

facts.claim: `ensure_schema(conn)` refuses to run when `public.events` exists, raising RuntimeError — the guard against creating the jobs tables inside the events database.
TABLE `jobs` — PK `id TEXT` (a truncated sha256, see make_id). Purpose: one row per posting from any source, deliberately unfiltered; ~2/3 of it is roles the pipeline exists to ignore.
TABLE `job_scores` — PK `(job_id, profile)`, job_id FK to jobs(id) ON DELETE/UPDATE CASCADE. Purpose: the per-profile LLM narrative (fit_score, gap_bridging_angle, risk_factors, scoring_model).
TABLE `profiles` — PK `profile TEXT`. Purpose: one cohort persona's persona_json / relevance_json / criteria_json plus criteria_version, daily_narrative_budget and active flag.
TABLE `job_facts` — PK `job_id TEXT` (single-column, FK to jobs). Purpose: the LLM-extracted properties of the POSTING, one row per posting ever, shared by all profiles.
TABLE `job_matches` — PK `(job_id, profile)`. Purpose: the arithmetic per-profile ranking (match_score, match_reasons) recomputed from job_facts; no LLM call.
TABLE `job_events` — PK `id BIGSERIAL`, plus profile/job_id/event/match_score/fit_score/occurred_at. Purpose: append-only engagement log; the pipeline reads it only in cohort.py.

TABLE `cohort_signal` — PK `(job_id, cohort_profile)`, with CHECK constraint `save_bucket IN ('3-5','6-10','10+')` generated from COHORT_BUCKET_LABELS. Purpose: the nightly-materialised, suppressed cohort save badge.
TABLE `hn_seen_comments` — PK `comment_id TEXT`. Purpose: hn-hiring.py's dedup ledger and the source of truth for 'this HN comment was already parsed'.
TABLE `google_jobs_query_stats` — PK `(slug, run_at)`. Purpose: append-only per-query run history for a not-yet-built adaptive-cadence feature; both Google scripts write it, nothing reads it.

TABLE `job_ingest_state` — PK `dataset TEXT`, created by `state.ensure_state_schema(conn, watermark_table='job_ingest_state', with_claims=True)`. Purpose: per-dataset watermark plus a TTL claim column.

TABLE `search_queries` — PK `id BIGSERIAL`, UNIQUE (normalized_text, normalized_location), CHECK on source in ('builder','seeded','track'). Purpose: the registered/seeded search catalogue the nightly dispatcher runs.
TABLE `search_query_watchers` — PK `(query_id, app_user_id)`; app_user_id is bare TEXT with no FK because app_users belongs to webapp/schema_web.py. Purpose: who watches which search.

TABLE `search_query_signal` — PK `(query_id, cohort_profile)`, CHECK on watcher_bucket in ('4-6','7-10','11+'). Purpose: the exposed, suppressed watcher-count bucket; the webapp role holds SELECT only.
TABLE `search_query_results` — PK `(query_id, job_id)`. Purpose: links a search to the postings it surfaced so the read endpoint JOINs jobs_app rather than re-running a text search.
VIEW `jobs_app` — created with CREATE OR REPLACE; ensure_app_view falls back to DROP+CREATE on psycopg.errors.InvalidTableDefinition, which silently discards every GRANT on the view.

jobs_app's guarantees over the base table: `j.status='open'` AND four `coalesce(...,'') <> ''` predicates on company_name, title, job_url and description_text, AND an INNER JOIN to job_matches — so an unranked posting cannot appear at all. Facts and scores are LEFT JOINed (scores additionally on s.profile = m.profile).
jobs_app column order is load-bearing: `f.role_track` must stay last, because CREATE OR REPLACE VIEW can only append and a reorder sends ensure_app_view down the DROP fallback that loses GRANTs.
jobs_app synthesises a `salary` column as `coalesce(j.salary_text, f.comp_currency || ' ' || nullif(concat_ws('-', f.comp_min, f.comp_max), ''))` — the only computed column in the view.

Extraction IS shared across profiles and scores ARE per profile, proven by the keys: job_facts declares `job_id TEXT PRIMARY KEY` with no profile column anywhere in its DDL, while job_scores and job_matches both declare `PRIMARY KEY (job_id, profile)`.
The staleness query for job_scores is score.py's `_STALE_ANY`: three arms, each guarded by IS NOT NULL and using `<>` rather than IS DISTINCT FROM so a NULL (unversioned) row is never stale.
`_STALE_FACTS` compares `s.facts_version <> f.facts_version` — the JOINED job_facts row, never schema.FACTS_VERSION. A test pins this.

criteria_version on job_scores is provenance only: it appears in no arm of _STALE_ANY, and test_a_criteria_bump_alone_does_not_make_a_score_stale asserts a bumped criteria_version selects nothing and leaves the row in the `current` census bucket.

criteria_version IS a cache key on job_matches: match_profile compares `(f['facts_version'], profile.criteria_version)` against `existing_versions()`'s `(facts_version, criteria_version)` tuple and skips the row when equal.

facts_version on job_facts is a cache key against the global constant, not a joined row: extract._eligible_sql selects `f.job_id IS NULL OR f.facts_version < %(version)s` where version = schema.FACTS_VERSION.

With both flags false, select_shortlist is exactly the old anti-join (`s.job_id IS NULL`); staleness only selects rows under the explicit --rescore-stale / --rescore-unversioned flags, and passing either without a ScoreContext raises ValueError.

add_missing_columns(conn, 'jobs', ...) adds `posted_at_ts TIMESTAMPTZ` and `salary_text TEXT`.
add_missing_columns(conn, 'job_facts', ...) adds `extraction_passes INTEGER`, `vote_unanimity REAL`, `role_track TEXT`.
add_missing_columns(conn, 'job_scores', ...) adds `facts_version INTEGER`, `persona_sha TEXT`, `prompt_version INTEGER`, `criteria_version INTEGER` — all nullable, no DEFAULT, nothing backfills them.

add_missing_columns(conn, 'job_events', ...) adds `request_id TEXT`, `rank INTEGER`, `dwell_ms INTEGER`, `reason TEXT`, `visibility TEXT DEFAULT 'private'`, `criteria_version INTEGER`, `app_user_id TEXT`. Only `visibility` takes a DEFAULT.
add_missing_columns also runs on the watermark table: `claimed_at TEXT` is added by ensure_state_schema(with_claims=True) and again defensively by state.try_claim on every call.

add_missing_columns exists to avoid `ADD COLUMN IF NOT EXISTS`, which still takes an ACCESS EXCLUSIVE lock even when it changes nothing; it reads information_schema.columns scoped to current_schema() first and returns the list actually added.

`UpsertResult` is a dataclass with four fields: new, updated, unchanged, errors (a list of truncated exception strings). `__iter__` returns `iter((self.new, self.updated, self.unchanged))` — exactly THREE values, and `.errors` is not among them.

Because __iter__ yields three values, `n, u, unc = upsert(...)` succeeds and silently discards every per-record failure; the comment records that eight call sites wrote it and a run that dropped a hundred records reported success with no alert and no non-zero exit.

`upsert_checked(*args, threshold=0.05, logger=None, **kwargs)` calls upsert(), ALWAYS logs `upsert-summary: table=… new=… updated=… unchanged=… errors=…` to stderr (even at errors=0, so the field's absence is the anomaly), then calls check_error_rate which raises UpsertErrorRate above the threshold. It returns the full UpsertResult including .errors.
upsert() commits before UpsertErrorRate is raised, so the successful records ARE written; the exception carries `.result` for callers that still want to accumulate them.

upsert() wraps each record in `with conn.transaction()` (a SAVEPOINT) rather than a plain try/except, because on Postgres a failed statement aborts the whole transaction and one bad row would otherwise lose the batch.
The three-branch rule: absent → INSERT (new); stored hash differs OR revive_column value != revive_value → UPDATE (updated); otherwise touch last_seen only (unchanged).

Sticky columns are read back from the stored row and substituted into the record BEFORE the content hash is computed, which is why the SELECT precedes the hash. GOOGLE_STICKY = ('posted_at','posted_at_ts') and only the Google sources are sticky.

lib/http.py's interface is get_bytes / get_text / get_json / post_json / urlencode, plus a TransientBody exception. get_bytes is the primitive because an XML document declaring its own encoding cannot be parsed from a str.

Over urlopen, lib/http adds: a default User-Agent 'hermes-ingest/1.0 (+https://github.com/hermes)', a 30s default timeout, 5 retries with exponential backoff `min(60, 2**attempt + uniform(0,1))` honouring Retry-After, retry on 429/5xx/URLError/TimeoutError/ConnectionError, immediate raise on any other HTTPError (401/400/404), and an optional `body_is_transient` predicate for upstreams that reject with HTTP 200 and an error page. There is NO rate limiting and no per-host throttle.

lib/http callers: ingest/ats.py (get_json/post_json), ingest/workday.py (get_text), ingest/weworkremotely.py (get_bytes, with its own browser-ish UA), ingest/builtin-nyc.py (get_text, and one deliberate max_retries=1 site), ingest/google-serpapi.py (get_json). D31 moved three of the four raw-urlopen sites onto it on 2026-08-02.

lib/ids.py exposes make_id(*parts, length=24) = sha256(':'.join(str(p)))[:24]; content_hash(rec, fields, blank_if_falsy=()) = sha256('|'.join(parts)); decode_google_job_id; normalize_apply_url; google_source_id.

What feeds a stored digest: `jobs.id` via schema.make_job_id → ids.make_id(platform, company_token, source_id); `jobs.content_hash` via ids.content_hash over the per-source HASH_FIELDS_* tuple. Order and membership of the tuple are part of the digest.

Four frozen per-source hash tuples: HASH_FIELDS_ATS (= _WWR) includes department and description_text; HASH_FIELDS_SHORT (Google, HN) drops department; HASH_FIELDS_BUILTIN uses seniority_guess and salary_text and NO description. salary_text is in the builtin hash but was not in COLUMNS until add_missing_columns landed it.

`blank_if_falsy=('description_text',)` is the compatibility hinge: the originals hashed `rec.get('description_text') or ''` while hashing every other field bare, so a missing description contributes '' and not the string 'None'.

google_source_id() returns htidocid when the base64 job_id blob yields one, else 'fp:' + sha256(company_token|lowercased title|normalized apply URL)[:16], deliberately excluding location because Google reports it inconsistently.

Also feeding stored digests indirectly: lib/text.strip_html and lib/text.posted_at_timestamp, named in lib/__init__.py as things that must never change without a deliberate rewrite across ~11,400 stored digests.

summary: The nightly path is `backend/run-daily.py`, which shells out to 14 sub-scripts in a fixed order (run-daily.py:124-241) — not the "nine steps" its own docstring repeats. Nine of those are ingest/discovery, then `searchqueries.py`, then the three scoring stages `extract.py` → `match.py` → `score.py`, then `cohort.py`. `relevance.py` is NOT a step: it has no `main()`, no `__main__` guard and no I/O at all — it is a pure SQL-string builder imported by extract.py, match.py and profiles.py that turns `config/relevance.json` (or a profile's `relevance_json`) into a `CASE ... THEN 1/2/3 END` tier expression (relevance.py:189-300) and a union-of-profiles boolean (relevance.py:307-334). So "the four stages" is really one library plus three executables. extract.py is the only place a posting becomes shared facts: it selects open, described, union-relevant jobs with no current-`FACTS_VERSION` job_facts row (extract.py:541-579), runs 1 or 3 LLM passes depending on `config/extraction-policy.json`'s per-platform measured agreement (extract.py:176-190), votes field-wise, and writes exactly one `job_facts` row per posting. match.py reads `job_facts JOIN jobs` (match.py:337-348), runs the pure `score_job()` (match.py:134-334) against each profile's `criteria_json`, and upserts `job_matches` rows that clear `schema.MATCH_FLOOR` (40), deleting demoted and orphaned ones. score.py orders that ranking by `m.match_score DESC` and spends `daily_narrative_budget` LLM calls per active profile writing `job_scores` narratives (score.py:418-482, 1016-1051). The user-facing order is `v.match_score DESC, coalesce(v.posted_at_ts,'-infinity') DESC, v.id ASC` in `backend/webapp/jobs.py:132` — `fit_score` appears nowhere in any ORDER BY. Deferral-vs-failure is decided by exception class in `llm.py`: `TransientError` (429/5xx/timeout/quota) writes nothing, everything else falls through to a tombstone row. Two sites cost LLM calls: extract.py:1058 and score.py:983. Version columns are `facts_version` (=3), `criteria_version` (per-profile integer), `persona_sha`, `prompt_version` (=1); `criteria_version` is recorded on `job_scores` but deliberately excluded from its staleness predicate.

extract.py loops batches (EXTRACT_BATCH_SIZE=40, EXTRACT_MAX_WORKERS=3) until drained, a 3600s monotonic deadline passes, or a batch makes zero progress (extracted+rejected==0). Deadline is checked between batches only and never before the first.

match.py reads job_facts JOIN jobs where j.status='open' AND f.extraction_model NOT LIKE 'FAILED:%' AND the relevance union — so tombstones and config-excluded postings are dropped at read time, not just at extraction time.

match.py writes job_matches (INSERT ... ON CONFLICT (job_id, profile) DO UPDATE) for rows scoring >= schema.MATCH_FLOOR, DELETEs rows that fell below the floor, and DELETEs orphans no longer in the loaded fact set. It makes zero LLM calls and zero network calls.

llm.py's production model default is DEFAULT_MODEL = 'deepseek-v4-flash'. It is a module constant, overridable by env: model() returns JOB_SCORING_MODEL or LLM_MODEL or DEFAULT_MODEL (on the 'claude' backend the fallback is 'claude-sonnet' instead).
JOBS_EXPECTED_MODEL, when set, makes extract.py and score.py refuse to start if the resolved model differs. Unset is a deliberate no-op.

HTTP transport defaults: base_url = JOB_SCORING_BASE_URL or LLM_BASE_URL or 'https://api.z.ai/api/paas/v4'; api_key = JOB_SCORING_API_KEY or LLM_API_KEY or GLM_API_KEY; timeout 120s; temperature 0; response_format={'type':'json_object'} when json_object is true.

On 429 / timeout / 5xx: llm raises TransientError. TRANSIENT_STATUSES = {408,409,425,429,500,502,503,504}; any URLError/TimeoutError/OSError (no response at all) is also TransientError; a ratelimit.QuotaExhausted raised before the request is converted to TransientError too.

On a non-transient HTTP status (e.g. 400/401/404) llm raises plain RuntimeError; on a 200 with no `choices` it raises RuntimeError. On a malformed-but-successful body, parse_json() returns None rather than raising.

The deferral-vs-tombstone branch in extract: `except llm.TransientError` sets transient=True and continues; `except (RuntimeError, json.JSONDecodeError)` continues without setting it. After the loop: usable passes -> EXTRACTED; else transient -> DEFERRED (nothing written); else -> REJECTED (tombstone).

The same branch in score: `except llm.TransientError -> return DEFERRED` (nothing written); `except (RuntimeError, json.JSONDecodeError) -> raw = None`, which falls through to mark_score_failed. A fourth outcome ERRORED (any other exception) also writes nothing.

A job_facts tombstone row is: job_id, facts_version = schema.FACTS_VERSION (current, not a sentinel), extracted_at = now, extraction_model = 'FAILED:<label>'. All 18 fact columns are left unset on insert; on conflict only those four columns are updated, so stale facts from a prior successful extraction are NOT cleared.

A job_scores tombstone row is: job_id, profile, scored_at = now, scoring_model = 'FAILED:<model>@<host>', plus all four version columns of the FAILED attempt. On conflict it explicitly NULLs fit_score, primary_track, gap_friendly_signal, key_technologies, gap_bridging_angle and risk_factors.

summary: `frontend/` is a complete, shipping, no-build ES-module client: one HTML shell (`frontend/index.html`), one hand-written stylesheet (`frontend/app.css`, 553 lines), and 13 `.mjs` modules under `frontend/js/`. Five screens exist and all five are reachable, all five call real endpoints, and all five render real payload data — there is no stub body, no TODO, and no placeholder screen anywhere in the client. `js/app.mjs` boots by calling `GET /v1/me`; a 401 or 403 paints a sign-in screen instead of the shell, otherwise it shows the topbar, nudges a never-onboarded Builder to `#/onboarding`, and hands off to a first-match-wins regex routing table (`app.mjs:120-137`) driven by `hashchange`. The four tabs in `index.html:45-48` (Today, Saved, Search, Profile) map one-to-one onto four rows of that table; the fifth route, `job`, is deliberately tabless and `check_client.mjs` asserts that the tabless set is exactly `["job"]`. The client calls fourteen distinct endpoint/method pairs and every one of them exists in `backend/webapp/` — nothing is called that the server does not route. Authentication is the session cookie alone: every fetch passes `credentials: "same-origin"` (not `"include"`), which is why `serve.py` mounts the static files onto the API's own process and port (`config.PORT`, default 8421) rather than a second dev server. Two screens do work the backend does not offer: Saved has no state filter on `GET /v1/jobs`, so it crawls up to 8×100 rows and filters `saved` client-side, and a cold deep link to a detail page triggers the same crawl purely to obtain a server-minted `request_id`. There is no npm, no `package.json`, no bundler and no `node_modules` anywhere under `frontend/` or at the repo root. Both checkers pass: `verify_fixtures.py` exits 0 with one line, `check_client.mjs` reports 54 checks, 0 failed.

The only navigation trigger is the hashchange listener registered in boot(); every in-client navigation is a bare `location.hash = ...` assignment, deliberately, so nothing paints twice.
Five routes exist: job (/^\/job\/(.+)$/), saved, search, onboarding, and the today fallback. Four have tabs; `job` is deliberately tabless.
check_client.mjs enforces the router/tab correspondence by parsing app.mjs's ROUTES literal and index.html's data-tab attributes as text, and asserts the set of routes with no tab is exactly ["job"].

Every fetch the client makes passes credentials: "same-origin" — not "include".

The task brief asks whether the client sends cookies with `credentials: 'include'`. It does not. dead_or_suspect.what: `let user = null;` is assigned from GET /v1/me and on sign-out, and never read anywhere.
dead_or_suspect.why: Dead state. The /v1/me response body is fetched and discarded — nothing in the client renders the signed-in Builder's email, name or profile. If a screen ever needs it, it is already in hand; today it is a no-op.

dead_or_suspect.what: `renders.forgetAll()` is exported and called by nothing.
dead_or_suspect.citation: frontend/js/renders.mjs:60-62 (grep -rn forgetAll frontend/js/ frontend/check_client.mjs returns only the definition)
dead_or_suspect.why: Landmine, not merely dead. signOut() (app.mjs:195-205) clears `user` and the hash but does NOT clear renders.mjs's `seen` Map or events.mjs's `impressed` Set. Sign out and sign in as a different Builder in the same tab and the detail page will attach the previous Builder's (request_id, rank) pair to the new Builder's events. Nothing in the suite covers a sign-out/sign-in cycle.

dead_or_suspect.what: `events.pending()` is exported and called by nothing in the client.
dead_or_suspect.why: Documented as a console/by-hand diagnostic. Harmless, but it is an exported surface with no caller and no test.

dead_or_suspect.what: POST /v1/events is spelled twice: once through api.postEvents and once as a hardcoded literal in the unload flush, with its own copy of credentials, keepalive and Content-Type.
dead_or_suspect.why: A second definition of an endpoint's path and options. Changing BASE, the path, or the credentials mode in api.mjs silently leaves the unload path behind — and the unload path is the one nobody watches in a browser, because the page is going away. The comment explains why fetch+keepalive rather than sendBeacon but not why the call bypasses api.mjs.

dead_or_suspect.what: Saved is a client-side filter over a full crawl, and a cold detail deep link triggers the same crawl purely to obtain a request_id.
dead_or_suspect.why: Both are recorded as backend gaps rather than client preferences, and both are bounded at 8×100. Today jobs_app holds ~166 rows for `pursuit` (crawl.mjs:28-31, measured 2026-08-02, unverifiable here without the DB), so it is two requests. At ten times the corpus, opening a pasted job link costs eight sequential 100-row requests before a single event can be sent, and Saved silently stops at 800.

dead_or_suspect.what: `credentials: "same-origin"` plus `BASE = ""` hard-couples the client to being served from the API's own origin.
dead_or_suspect.why: The failure mode is exactly the one this repo alerts on: served from any other host, every request goes out without the session cookie and comes back 401, which the client renders as the sign-in screen. It is indistinguishable from being logged out, and there is no error text anywhere. serve.py's warn_about_origins covers the CORS and FRONTEND_ORIGIN cases but not this one, because this one is not a CORS failure.

dead_or_suspect.what: `ui.cssEscape` reaches for `window.CSS` while every other module uses bare globals.
dead_or_suspect.why: `window` is undefined under node. check_client.mjs stubs `globalThis.CSS` (check_client.mjs:50) but never `window`, so this path would throw a ReferenceError if any check called paintSaved. None does — the function is exercised only in a browser, so the fallback branch is untested.

dead_or_suspect.what: The onboarding preferences are stored and filter nothing.

area: webapp — backend/webapp/, the browser-facing FastAPI service (jobs list, events, searches, onboarding, labelling, Google SSO)
summary: `backend/webapp/` is a FastAPI app assembled in `app.py` from five routers (auth, jobs, search, onboarding, label) plus one inline `/v1/health` route — 19 routes total, all under `/v1/`. Authentication is Google OAuth 2.0 Authorization Code + PKCE driven entirely server-side (`auth.py`); the browser only ever receives an opaque session token in a cookie whose sha256 is what `app_sessions` stores. Google authenticates; the `app_users` allowlist authorises, and a valid Google login for an address with no row is a 403 that creates nothing. Every authenticated route depends on `require_user`, which re-joins `app_sessions` to `app_users` on every request (so `profile`, `active` and `is_admin` are re-read each time) and slides the expiry forward once past half-TTL. Tenancy is `user.profile` from the session — there is no `?profile=` parameter anywhere. Reads go through the `jobs_app` view in `../schema.py`; the single exception is `label.py:127`, which reads the base `jobs` table on purpose because gate-rejected postings have no `job_facts` row and so cannot appear in the view. The ranked list is ordered by `v.match_score DESC, coalesce(v.posted_at_ts,'-infinity') DESC, v.id ASC` (`jobs.py:132`); `fit_score` is selected but never sorted on, and no LLM call exists anywhere in this process — the venv installs five packages and the only outbound HTTP is `httpx` POSTing Google's token endpoint. Writes are narrow and enforced by GRANT: `job_events` and `eval_labels` are INSERT-only (append-only evidence), `builder_job_state`/`builder_profiles`/`search_query_watchers` are upsert-or-null-out with no DELETE, and both aggregate tables (`cohort_signal`, `search_query_signal`) are SELECT-only so this service cannot write a suppression bucket it did not compute. `schema_web.py:718 verify_schema()` refuses to boot unless every table, sequence, added column and `app_users.profile → profiles` mapping checks out. The webapp suite is green at 352 tests.

facts.claim: The app is FastAPI with docs_url=None/redoc_url=None and a lifespan that calls schema_web.verify_schema(conn) before serving; a missing GRANT is a startup error, not a 500 on first click.

Five routers are included in this order: auth, jobs, search, onboarding, label; jobs.ContractError's handler is registered between search and onboarding so both produce the {"error":{code,message,request_id}} envelope.
There are exactly 19 routed endpoints (18 on routers + /v1/health).
Authentication is a session COOKIE, not a bearer header and not client-side Google SSO. The cookie value is `secrets.token_urlsafe(32)`; only its sha256 is stored, in app_sessions.token_hash.

The session is minted in GET /v1/auth/callback after a server-side token exchange, by INSERT INTO app_sessions (token_hash, user_id, created_at, expires_at, last_seen_at, revoked_at, user_agent, ip) plus an UPDATE of app_users.last_login_at.

The session is verified in require_user by one query joining app_sessions to app_users on token_hash; revoked_at → 401 'session revoked', expires_at <= now → 401 'session expired', active FALSE → 403 'account disabled'.

Session lifetime is SESSION_TTL_DAYS, default 30, and it slides: if the remaining life is under half the full TTL, expires_at and last_seen_at are pushed forward on that request (at most one write per half-TTL).

Cookie attributes: name SESSION_COOKIE_NAME (default "jobs_session"), max_age = SESSION_TTL_DAYS*24*3600, httponly=True, secure=config.SESSION_COOKIE_SECURE (default True), samesite="lax", path="/". Lax rather than Strict because the OAuth callback is a top-level cross-site navigation.
SESSION_COOKIE_SECURE is parsed by _flag(), where an unrecognised value falls back to the default (True) rather than to False — a typo cannot silently disable it.

The id_token's signature is NOT verified; only aud, iss, exp (±60s skew), nonce, sub, email and email_verified are checked on the decoded payload, and that is sound only because the token comes straight out of our own TLS+client-secret-authenticated POST to Google's token endpoint.
PKCE state, verifier, nonce and next_path live in the oauth_logins table, redeemed single-use with DELETE ... RETURNING, so replay protection is a property of the primary key.
User resolution matches google_sub first, then falls back to (email AND google_sub IS NULL) to bind the sub on first login; no row is ever created by login, and an un-allowlisted address gets 403.

safe_next_path() reduces any caller-supplied `next` to a local path with an allowlist (one leading slash, no '//', no ':' before '?', no backslash, no control chars) and silently returns '/' otherwise. It gates both the login parameter and the post-callback redirect.
CORS: allow_origins=config.ALLOWED_ORIGINS (never '*'), allow_credentials=True, allow_methods=["GET","POST","OPTIONS"], allow_headers=["Content-Type"].

ALLOWED_ORIGINS is a comma-split env var whose literal default is "http://localhost:5173"; FRONTEND_ORIGIN's literal default is also "http://localhost:5173" (rstrip'd of trailing '/'). GOOGLE_REDIRECT_URI defaults to "http://localhost:8421/v1/auth/callback".
The ranked list's ordering is ORDER BY v.match_score DESC, coalesce(v.posted_at_ts,'-infinity'::timestamptz) DESC, v.id ASC — one constant shared by /v1/jobs and /v1/searches/{id}/results.
facts.citation: backend/webapp/jobs.py:131-132; used at backend/webapp/jobs.py:491 and backend/webapp/search.py:365

facts.claim: fit_score is only a selected column (position 30 of LIST_COLUMNS) and appears in no ORDER BY in this package; it annotates, it does not sort.

No LLM call sits between a request and an ordering, and none exists in this process at all: requirements.txt is fastapi, uvicorn[standard], psycopg[binary], pydantic, httpx, and the only httpx call in the package is the POST to Google's token endpoint.

match_score comes from job_matches via the jobs_app view, written offline by match.py; fit_score comes from job_scores. The view is jobs JOIN job_matches LEFT JOIN job_facts LEFT JOIN job_scores, filtered to status open and non-empty company_name/title/job_url/description_text.

Every job read in jobs.py and search.py is FROM jobs_app; the only query against the base `jobs` table in the whole package is label.py's _job(), deliberately, because gate-rejected postings have no job_facts row and so cannot appear in the view.
schema_web.REQUIRED_TABLES nonetheless grants SELECT on `jobs` because a plain view runs with the CALLER's privileges and is not a security barrier.
A request picks its profile from app_users.profile, carried on the session User dataclass; there is no profile request parameter on any route.

app_users.profile is NOT NULL with no FK to profiles(profile); the missing FK is compensated at write time (manage_app_users add/set-profile via profiles.load_one), at deploy time (profile_mapping_problems in verify_schema) and at request time (POST /v1/onboarding 400 'unknown_profile').

POST /v1/events INSERTs into job_events selecting from job_matches: (profile, app_user_id, job_id, event, request_id, rank, dwell_ms, reason, visibility, match_score, fit_score, criteria_version, occurred_at). rank IS recorded, taken from the client and required for 'impression' and 'open'.

match_score, fit_score, criteria_version, visibility and app_user_id are all server-side: match_score/criteria_version off the job_matches row, fit_score by subquery on job_scores, visibility from visibility_for(), app_user_id from user.id. None is accepted from the client.
Client-sendable events are impression, open, save, unsave, dismiss, undismiss, applied; 'skip' is server-derived only and a client sending it gets code 'server_derived_event'.

Impressions are deduplicated for 24 hours on (profile, job_id) — deliberately NOT narrowed to app_user_id, which the code records as an open owner decision with the consequence that one Builder's render suppresses another's impression of the same job for the window.

An 'open' triggers derive_skips(), which INSERTs 'skip' rows copying profile/app_user_id/request_id/rank/match_score/fit_score/criteria_version from the un-actioned impressions above that rank in the same render, scoped by imp.app_user_id = caller and vetoed only by the caller's own non-impression events (defect D68's two halves).
save/unsave/dismiss/undismiss additionally upsert builder_job_state keyed (app_user_id, job_id) in the same transaction; impression/open/applied write no state row at all.
Only 'save' is cohort-visible; every other event is stored visibility='private', including 'applied'.
The per-row state fields seen/applied are derived from job_events by app_user_id (never by profile), and dismissed/saved/dismiss_reason come from builder_job_state — the fix for defects D66/D67.
GET /v1/jobs hides dismissed rows by default (bs.dismissed_at IS NULL) and GET /v1/jobs/{id} deliberately does not, so undo stays reachable.

Pagination is an opaque base64 keyset cursor at CURSOR_VERSION 2 carrying (match_score, posted_at_ts, job_id, request_id, next_rank); a v1 cursor is rejected with 400 'malformed cursor' rather than upgraded, so `rank` stays global across pages of one render.
The cohort save badge is read from the materialised cohort_signal table (save_bucket only, never computed_at, never counted live from job_events); a suppressed posting has no row and renders as null.
schema.COHORT_MIN_SAVERS = 3 and schema.SEARCH_MIN_WATCHERS = 4 are the suppression thresholds those buckets implement.

Search results reuse jobs.py's LIST_COLUMNS, joins, ORDER_BY, cursor and field order verbatim by import, so /v1/jobs and /v1/searches/{id}/results are byte-for-byte the same response shape apart from the added query_id.
A Builder may watch at most searchnorm.MAX_QUERIES_PER_BUILDER = 20 searches; exceeding it is ContractError 'too_many_searches'. Default location is 'New York, NY'.
Unwatch is POST (not DELETE) specifically because the CORS middleware allows only GET/POST/OPTIONS, and it UPDATEs removed_at rather than deleting the row.

search_query_watchers never reaches a response; only sig.watcher_bucket and a boolean 'watching' for the caller's own row are exposed, and first_requested_at is excluded from QUERY_COLUMNS on purpose.

POST /v1/onboarding writes app_users.prior_domain (only when supplied), upserts builder_profiles with coalesce-preserve semantics, derives tracks from job_scores.primary_track, then calls jobs.record_events() in a SEPARATE transaction to write the seed judgements as real job_events.
Seed verdicts map 'interested'→save and 'not_interested'→dismiss, with no reason attached.

Onboarding vocabularies are shared with the generated CHECK constraints: PRIOR_DOMAINS (10 values incl. 'other' and 'none'), SITUATIONS (4), LOCATION_PREFS ('nyc','remote','either'), REMOTE_PREFS ('onsite_ok','hybrid_ok','remote_only'), SCHEDULE_CONSTRAINTS ('no_overnight',).
GET /v1/label is the only route that does not 401 a signed-out caller: it calls require_user() manually and converts a 401 into a 302 to /v1/auth/login?next=/v1/label (a 403 still propagates).

POST /v1/label parses the urlencoded body with urllib.parse rather than request.form(), caps it at 64 KiB (413), rejects a non-urlencoded Content-Type with 415, verifies the posting is in eval_label_items, re-checks round-2 preconditions server-side, and 303s back to /v1/label.
Labelling records app_users.id as labeller_id and never the email; profile is attached only on axis B rows, from the session.

verify_schema checks table existence, per-table privileges via has_table_privilege, sequence privileges (job_events_id_seq, search_queries_id_seq, eval_labels_id_seq), added columns on job_events and eval_labels, and orphan app_users.profile values — accumulating all problems into one RuntimeError.

The service's declared privileges are read-only on every pipeline table except job_events (SELECT+INSERT), search_queries (SELECT+INSERT) and search_query_watchers (SELECT+INSERT+UPDATE); cohort_signal, search_query_signal and search_query_results are SELECT-only by design so the service cannot write an aggregate it did not compute.
config.py performs the sys.path insert of backend/ (one level up) at import, which is why every module in the package imports `config` first.

The package imports pipeline top-level modules: lib.envfile, lib.dbconn, lib.timeparse, schema, profiles, searchnorm and evals.labels. It imports NOTHING from api/, and nothing in backend/ or backend/api/ imports webapp.

The venv is isolated: backend/webapp/.venv/pyvenv.cfg sets include-system-site-packages = false on python 3.14.6, so schema.py/lib/ are reachable only via the sys.path insert and nothing else is importable.
config.PORT defaults to 8421 and is annotated 'Documentation only -- uvicorn takes --port'; nothing in the webapp binds it. frontend/serve.py is what actually passes it to uvicorn.run().

frontend/serve.py imports the same `app` object and mounts StaticFiles at "/" with html=True AFTER every router, adding a GET / (and static file) surface to this same process when it is the entry point.

backend/webapp/.env contains exactly 8 uncommented keys: DATABASE_URL, GOOGLE_CLIENT_ID, GOOGLE_CLIENT_SECRET, GOOGLE_REDIRECT_URI, FRONTEND_ORIGIN, ALLOWED_ORIGINS, SESSION_COOKIE_SECURE, JOBS_ADMIN_DATABASE_URL. (Values not read out.)
manage_app_users.py is a CLI, not a route surface: init-schema, add, set-profile, list, disable, enable, sessions, revoke-sessions. init-schema is the only DDL path and uses JOBS_ADMIN_DATABASE_URL.
The webapp test suite is green: 352 tests, OK.

contradictions: The invariant as written in the code — backend/schema.py:617, 'they share only this file and lib/, and none imports another' — is only half true. webapp/ imports FOUR pipeline top-level modules beyond schema.py and lib/: `profiles` (onboarding.py:54, manage_app_users.py:63), `searchnorm` (search.py:55), `schema` (schema_web.py:29, search.py:54) and `evals.labels` (label.py:68, schema_web.py:156). The part that IS true: webapp imports nothing from api/, api imports nothing from webapp, and no pipeline module imports webapp (verified by grep across backend/*.py and backend/api/*.py). So 'the three processes do not import each other' holds between api/ and webapp/, but webapp/ does import the pipeline process's own modules, not merely the two shared ones.

The brief says to report the port the service 'binds by default'. Strictly, the webapp binds nothing: config.PORT (backend/webapp/config.py:124) defaults to 8421 but is annotated 'Documentation only -- uvicorn takes --port', and app.py has no __main__ / uvicorn.run(). The only code that turns config.PORT into a bind is frontend/serve.py:162,177, which is in a different directory and a different entry point. 8421 is correct as an answer, but it comes from an env-var default plus a launcher, not from the service.

entrypoints.name: GET /v1/health
entrypoints.description: No auth. Liveness only, deliberately no database call. Returns {"ok": true}.

entrypoints.name: GET /v1/auth/login
entrypoints.description: No auth. 503 if GOOGLE_CLIENT_ID/SECRET unset. Mints state+nonce+PKCE verifier, INSERTs oauth_logins (with safe_next_path(next)), 302s to accounts.google.com with scope 'openid email profile' and prompt=select_account.

entrypoints.name: GET /v1/auth/callback
entrypoints.description: No auth (this is what creates it). Redeems oauth_logins single-use with DELETE..RETURNING, prunes expired logins, POSTs Google's token endpoint over httpx, validates id_token claims incl. nonce, resolves/refuses the app_users row (403 if not allowlisted or inactive), INSERTs app_sessions, UPDATEs app_users.last_login_at, sets the session cookie and 302s to FRONTEND_ORIGIN + next_path. 400 on missing/unknown/expired state, 502 if Google unreachable, 401 on any token or claim failure (reason logged, never returned).

entrypoints.name: POST /v1/auth/logout
entrypoints.description: Cookie optional. UPDATEs app_sessions.revoked_at where token_hash matches and revoked_at IS NULL, deletes the cookie repeating path/httponly/secure/samesite, returns {"ok": true} with 200 even when there was no session.

entrypoints.name: GET /v1/me
entrypoints.description: require_user. Touches no jobs table — returns {email, display_name, profile, is_admin} straight off the session join.

entrypoints.name: GET /v1/jobs
entrypoints.description: require_user. Params: limit (1..100, default 25), cursor, q (ILIKE title/company), remote, nyc, min_score, since, include_dismissed (default false). Reads jobs_app LEFT JOIN LATERAL job_events (by app_user_id) LEFT JOIN builder_job_state LEFT JOIN cohort_signal, WHERE v.profile = session profile. Returns {request_id, jobs[35 view columns + seen, applied, dismissed, saved, dismiss_reason + cohort_signal + rank], next_cursor, profile}.

entrypoints.name: GET /v1/jobs/{job_id}
entrypoints.description: require_user. Same joins plus description_text; does NOT filter dismissals so undo stays reachable. 404 'no such job for this profile' when the row is absent or belongs to another profile (deliberately indistinguishable).

entrypoints.name: POST /v1/events
entrypoints.description: require_user. Body {events: [{job_id, event, rank?, dwell_ms?, reason?}] (max 200), request_id}. validate_batch fails the WHOLE batch on unknown/server-derived event, missing request_id, missing rank on impression/open, reason on a non-dismiss or outside DISMISS_REASONS, dwell_ms on a non-open. Writes job_events (+builder_job_state, +derived skips) in one transaction. Returns {recorded, deduped, skipped, derived_skips}.
entrypoints.invoked_by: frontend client; also called in-process by onboarding.record_seed_judgements

entrypoints.name: POST /v1/searches
entrypoints.description: require_user. Body {text, location?, chips?}. Normalises via searchnorm.validate (400 in the contract envelope on InvalidQuery), enforces the 20-watch cap, find-or-creates search_queries in one statement, registers the caller as a watcher, returns the query row with watcher_bucket and watching. No provider is called — registration is asynchronous.

entrypoints.name: GET /v1/searches
entrypoints.description: require_user. scope=mine|suggested (regex-pinned), limit 1..100. 'mine' = rows the caller watches; 'suggested' = source IN ('seeded','track') AND retired_at IS NULL. There is deliberately no third 'everything' scope. Returns {searches, scope}.

entrypoints.name: GET /v1/searches/{query_id}
entrypoints.description: require_user. One query row + bucket + own watch state; 404 'no such search' rather than 403.

entrypoints.name: POST /v1/searches/{query_id}/watch
entrypoints.description: require_user. 404 if the query does not exist; cap-checked; INSERTs/reactivates the watcher row; returns the query row.

entrypoints.name: POST /v1/searches/{query_id}/unwatch
entrypoints.description: require_user. POST not DELETE because CORS allows only GET/POST/OPTIONS. UPDATEs removed_at; returns the query row.

entrypoints.name: GET /v1/searches/{query_id}/results
entrypoints.description: require_user. jobs_app JOIN search_query_results plus the same three state joins and the same ORDER_BY and cursor as /v1/jobs. Returns {request_id, query_id, jobs[...], next_cursor, profile}. Never reads the `jobs` table or search_query_results alone, so relevance gating is structural.

entrypoints.name: GET /v1/onboarding
entrypoints.description: require_user. Reads app_users LEFT JOIN builder_profiles; returns {onboarding:{completed, completed_at, prior_domain, prior_years}, profile}.

entrypoints.name: POST /v1/onboarding
entrypoints.description: require_user. Body has prior_domain, prior_years, situation, location_pref, remote_pref, comp_floor, schedule_constraints, seed_judgements (max 40); every field optional, all validated in the handler into the contract's 400 envelope. 400 'unknown_profile' if the session's profile has no `profiles` row. Writes app_users.prior_domain, upserts builder_profiles, then writes seed judgements through jobs.record_events in a second transaction. Returns {onboarding, seed_judgements_recorded, profile}.

entrypoints.name: GET /v1/label
entrypoints.description: Server-rendered HTML. Signed-out → 302 to /v1/auth/login?next=/v1/label instead of 401. ?round=1|2 (allowlist of two), ?blank=1. Reads the active eval label set, next unlabelled item, progress, and the posting from the base `jobs` table; renders a no-JavaScript radio form with an explicit 'I can't tell' abstention per question.
entrypoints.invoked_by: a Builder volunteer pasting a link

entrypoints.name: POST /v1/label
entrypoints.description: require_user (401 JSON, no redirect). Manual urlencoded parse, 413 over 64 KiB, 415 on wrong content type, 404 if the posting is not in the label set, 400 on round-2 violations. Writes eval_labels via evals.labels.record with labeller_id=user.id; 303 back to /v1/label (carrying round, and blank=1 if nothing was written).

entrypoints.name: GET /v1/label/progress
entrypoints.description: require_user. JSON {label_set, done, total} for the caller only.

entrypoints.name: GET / and static assets (only under frontend/serve.py)

summary: `backend/api/` is a small FastAPI service that lets untrusted volunteers spend their OWN SerpApi credits on the operator's behalf. It exposes four routes on 127.0.0.1:8420: an unauthenticated `/v1/health`, and three bearer-authenticated endpoints that hand out (`claim`), accept results for (`submit`) and give back (`release`) a lock on one Google-Jobs query slug from `backend/config/google-queries.json`. Auth is `sha256(bearer)` looked up in `api_keys`; raw keys are never stored and revoked rows are kept. Everything a contributor sends is re-derived server-side by the pipeline's own `google_jobs.normalize_job` and written through `lib.upsert` with the pipeline's `TableSpec`, so API-written `jobs` rows are byte-identical to locally-ingested ones. The claim is a conditional `INSERT … ON CONFLICT … DO UPDATE … WHERE claimed_at IS NULL OR claimed_at < ttl_cutoff RETURNING dataset` on the *shared* `job_ingest_state` row, plus a `claim_granted_at` snapshot that detects the pipeline stealing an expired claim out from under a contributor. It runs as its own restricted Postgres role `jobs_api` in the same `jobs` database and `public` schema as the pipeline, with SELECT/INSERT/UPDATE on exactly six tables and nothing on `job_scores`/`job_facts`/`job_matches`/`jobs_app` — verified live. Its venv sets `include-system-site-packages = false`, and system `python3` genuinely cannot import `app.py` (no `fastapi`). facts.claim: Double-claiming is prevented by a single conditional upsert on `job_ingest_state`: `ON CONFLICT (dataset) DO UPDATE SET claimed_at=…, claimed_by=…, claim_granted_at=… WHERE job_ingest_state.claimed_at IS NULL OR job_ingest_state.claimed_at < ttl_cutoff RETURNING dataset`. Only one racer gets a row back.

`holds_claim` requires three things simultaneously: `claimed_by == contributor_id`, `claim_granted_at == claimed_at` (nobody re-claimed since this service granted it), and `claimed_at >= now - CLAIM_TTL_MINUTES`. The middle condition is the guard against the pipeline stealing an expired claim and leaving `claimed_by` stale.

Claim lifecycle terminals: `mark_success` sets `last_success_at` and NULLs all three claim columns in one statement; `release_claim` NULLs the three claim columns and leaves the watermark alone; otherwise the claim simply expires after CLAIM_TTL_MINUTES.
CLAIM_TTL_MINUTES defaults to 15 and GOOGLE_JOBS_MIN_HOURS_BETWEEN_RUNS to 20; both are read from the environment and are independent constants from the pipeline's.

An empty submission (`{"jobs": []}`) does NOT advance the watermark: it releases the claim, writes a `submit` log row with reason 'empty submission -- watermark not advanced', and returns `watermark_advanced: False`.

Submit reads the raw body and enforces the 2 MiB cap BEFORE pydantic parsing (413), then parses manually so a malformed body yields 400 with a detail built only from whitelisted identifier tokens — no byte of the request body reaches the response.
Submitting against a dataset you do not hold a live claim on is 409, not 403; a slug absent from the server's query bank is also 409; an unreadable query bank is 500 on both `claim` and `submit`.

`mode` (which drives the remote heuristic) is looked up from the server's own query bank, never taken from the request, and every stored field is recomputed by `qc.normalize_job`, which is re-exported from the pipeline's `google_jobs.py`.

Writes to `jobs` go through `lib.upsert.upsert_checked` with `schema.google_spec()` and `schema.make_job_id` — the same code path the pipeline's ingest scripts use — and `UpsertErrorRate` is caught rather than propagated so a partially-written batch is reported, not 500'd after the write.
There is exactly one writer of `submission_log` (`qc.log_submission`), it rejects any action outside the closed vocabulary ('claim','submit','release'), and it deliberately does not commit.

summary: Nine ingest scripts run under `backend/run-daily.py`, all of them writing normalized postings into the single `jobs` table via `lib.upsert.upsert_checked` and recording watermarks/claims in `job_ingest_state`. Seven reach real network endpoints tonight: `ingest/ats.py` (six ATS platforms — Greenhouse, Lever, Ashby, Workable, Recruitee, SmartRecruiters — roster read from the `company_ats` table, not a config file), `ingest/workday.py` (Workday CXS, POST list + per-posting detail, gated upstream so only survivors get a detail fetch), `ingest/builtin-nyc.py` (HTML scrape + JSON-LD detail pages), `ingest/nyc-open-data.py` (Socrata SODA, optional app token), `ingest/weworkremotely.py` (four category RSS feeds), `ingest/hn-hiring.py` (HN Firebase API, one monthly thread) and the two Google Jobs scripts (`google-serpapi.py`, `google-apify.py`) that share one query bank and one claim scheme. `ingest/ats_sources.py` is a library, not a script — it turns `company_ats` rows into a deduped roster and holds the retired `--seed-from-json` path. A tenth ingest-shaped step, `searchqueries.py`, dispatches Builder search queries through `backend/serp/`. The bare-`upsert()` three-tuple defect is fully closed: every write in `backend/ingest/` goes through `upsert_checked`, and two tests assert it by reading source text. `backend/serp/` is a real seam with exactly two provider adapters (serpapi, apify), a router (`ORDER`), a disk cache keyed on date+chip but never on the API key, and a quota ledger whose authority is the vendor's own counter — but it is reached only by `searchqueries.py`; the two legacy Google ingest scripts still carry their own copies of the same fetch logic and bypass it entirely. Reconciliation against an API-reported `total` exists in exactly three places (ats.py's `Fetched.complete`, workday.py's `Shortfall`, nyc-open-data.py's `reconcile()`), and in every case a failed reconciliation suppresses closure rather than being shrugged off.

Workday's page-size ceiling is the literal MAX_PAGE_LIMIT = 20, with PAGE_LIMIT = MAX_PAGE_LIMIT. _check_page_limit() raises LimitTooLarge rather than clamping, and is called from list_body(), which every request path goes through.

workday.py reconciles collected postings against the API's `total` and raises Shortfall, but the check is not equality — the threshold is one page (`deficit >= limit`), because a board moving mid-walk (Nordstrom: total=867, 865 collected on 2026-07-28) would otherwise cost the largest boards whole nights.

workday.py reads `total` from the offset=0 page ONLY (`if total is None: total = payload.get("total")`) because every later page answers total: 0 — measured against msk.wd108, total=88 at offset 0 and 0 at offsets 20/40/60/80.
workday.py also guards against Workday returning the FIRST page again for an out-of-range offset (`fresh == 0` wrap guard); without it the loop cycles forever against a live tenant.

ats.py's only closure call is gated on three conditions: non-empty records, `fetched.complete`, and not a --delta run on a delta-capable platform. A short fetch is reported in `unreconciled` instead.

backend/serp/ implements exactly TWO providers: PROVIDERS = {serpapi, apify}, ORDER = (serpapi, apify), cheapest-renewable first. resolve() raises ValueError on an unknown name rather than falling back, because six of eight planned adapters were cut.

dispatch.py chooses nothing between providers itself — it resolves one provider (from `provider=` arg, else SEARCH_QUERY_PROVIDER env, else ORDER[0]) and binds it for the whole run. There is no per-query fallthrough despite ORDER being described as 'the router's fallthrough order'.

quota.py's Ledger.check() asks the VENDOR's own counter (mod.account(creds)) and raises ProviderRefused when `left - reserve <= 0`. When the vendor is unreachable it ALLOWS the run and records the unavailability.

quota.reconcile() compares vendor-billed-over-this-run (closing read minus opening read) against the within-run local tally, not month-scale totals; Apify is `reconcilable: false` so its delta is always None and reported as 'NOT RECONCILED'.

serp.call() enforces cache-before-ledger-before-fetch, and a cached answer is returned with credits=0 and from_cache=True; cost_line() then refuses to report cost or latency for any run containing a cached answer.
The serp cache key is (normalized query, location, date_chip, provider, date) with a 24h TTL and explicitly excludes the API key.

summary: `backend/evals/` is a self-contained measurement package that runs the pipeline's two LLM stages (extract, score) against frozen JSONL fixtures instead of production, and turns the results into numbers. The chain is: `corpus.py` freezes postings (per-platform `ROW_NUMBER()`, never a global recency slice) → `tasks/{extract,score}.py` adapt the REAL `extract.py`/`score.py` prompt+normalize into a task object → `runner.py` executes N passes through `llm.call_detailed` with a ThreadPoolExecutor → `metrics.py` computes agreement and ranking arithmetic → `report.py` renders/serialises. `metrics.field_cell()` emits FOUR distinct per-field agreement quantities — `agree2`, `unanimous`, `pairwise` and (sets only) `jaccard` — plus a fifth record-level `whole_record` rate; `--repeat N` is a run parameter that sets how many passes feed those functions, never a metric. facts.claim: There are FOUR distinct per-field self-consistency quantities computed in one place, `metrics.field_cell()`, and their exact code names are `agree2`, `unanimous`, `pairwise`, `jaccard`. All four are emitted from the same dict literal.

`agree2` = agree2_k / n, where agree2_k counts records for which `exact(kind, values[0], values[1])` — i.e. repeat 1 against repeat 2 ONLY, ignoring repeats 3..N. Its 95% Wilson interval is emitted beside it as `agree2_ci`.

`unanimous` = unan_k / n, where unan_k counts records for which `_identical(kind, values)` is true; `_identical` is `all(exact(kind, values[0], v) for v in values[1:])` — every one of the N repeats exactly equal. Interval `unanimous_ci` is Wilson.

`pairwise` = (1/n) * sum over records of [ mean over all C(N,2) repeat pairs of the 0/1 indicator `exact(kind,a,b)` ]. It is a mean-of-means (per-record mean first, then across records), NOT a pooled pair rate, and it deliberately carries NO confidence interval because pairs from one record are not independent trials.

`jaccard` is a FIFTH column that exists only when kind == 'set': (1/n) * sum over records of the mean pairwise `jaccard(a,b)`. It is graded [0,1], unlike the three headline columns which are 0/1 exact-match even for sets — the reason given is that a table mixing a graded and an exact column for the same field is unreadable.

A sixth, record-level quantity `whole_record` = k/n over records where EVERY non-prose field is `_identical` across all N repeats. `prose` kinds (e.g. `summary`, `gap_bridging_angle`) are skipped via `skip_kinds=('prose',)` — including them would make it 0 by construction.

`exact(kind,a,b)` is `compare(kind,a,b) == 1.0`, and `compare` returns `jaccard(a,b)` for kind 'set' and `1.0 if a == b else 0.0` otherwise. So None == None scores as AGREEMENT for enums/ints/bools — which `labels.as_model_domain()` explicitly depends on for `role_track`.

`--repeat N` is a RUN PARAMETER, not a metric. Argument parser: `sc.add_argument("--repeat", type=int, default=3, help="passes over the corpus; 3 gives a majority")`. It only exists on the `selfcheck` subcommand.

Proof that --repeat is a run parameter, part 2: it is validated (`< 2` → print FAILED, return 2), then passed straight to `runner.run_repeated(repeat=args.repeat)`, which loops `for i in range(repeat)` calling `run()` sequentially. No metric function anywhere takes a `repeat` argument — `field_cell()` takes per-record value TUPLES whose arity happens to be N.
The only place the repeat count surfaces in output is `stats['repeat'] = len(runs)` — a run descriptor sitting beside the metrics, not one of them.

`average_precision(scores, labels, *, ties='expected')` returns a `Ranked` 5-tuple, not a scalar. `.value = total / n_pos`. Rows with score None are dropped by `_score_blocks` and counted out separately as `n_dropped` / `n_dropped_positive`. `.value` is None when there are no positives.

average_precision implements three tie policies. `optimistic`: `total += sum((rel_above+m)/(above+m) for m in 1..rel)`. `pessimistic`: `total += sum((rel_above+m)/(above+size-rel+m) for m in 1..rel)`. `expected` (default): for j in 1..size, `ahead = 1.0 if size==1 else 1.0 + (j-1)*(rel-1)/(size-1)` and `total += (rel/size)*(rel_above+ahead)/(above+j)` — the McSherry & Najork (2008) O(n) closed form, cited in the source.

`precision_at_k(scores, labels, k=TOP_K)` uses `kk = min(k, n)` and walks the tie blocks: `take = min(size, slots); hits += rel*take/size`. Returns `hits/kk`. Fractional numerators are correct by design, not rounding errors. `k <= 0` yields value None (a real config: pursuit's daily_narrative_budget is 0).

TOP_K = 20, justified in the source by score.py's daily_narrative_budget default and by CLAUDE.md naming precision@20 as the objective; SCORE_TOLERANCES = (0, 5, 10) and all three bands are always reported, never one.
`wilson(k, n, z=Z95)` with Z95 = 1.959963984540054 returns (0.0, 1.0) for n <= 0 rather than raising; centre = (p + z²/2n)/(1 + z²/n), half = (z/denom)*sqrt(p(1-p)/n + z²/4n²), clamped to [0,1].

`spearman(xs, ys)` returns (rho, n) over positions where BOTH are non-None, using average (tie-sharing) ranks from `_ranks()`; returns rho=None when fewer than 2 pairs or either side is constant. `top_k_overlap(ids, xs, ys, k)` returns |top-k ∩ top-k| / min(k, rows), ties broken deterministically by str(job_id).

`ranking()` is the score-field block: mean and MIN Spearman rho over all repeat pairs, mean and min top-20 overlap, mean/max absolute diff, and tolerance bands at ±0/±5/±10 with Wilson CIs. The min is reported because a mean hides one unstable pass.

`bootstrap_delta()` is a paired bootstrap comparing two orderings against the same labels: BOOTSTRAP_DRAWS=2000, CI_LEVEL=0.95, BOOTSTRAP_SEED=11, MIN_USABLE_FRACTION=0.5 (below which it returns value=None rather than an interval). One resample index list is used for BOTH orderings, which is what makes it paired.

`labels.inter_annotator()` (the CEILING) and `labels.intra_annotator()` reuse `metrics.field_cell()` UNCHANGED, so agree2/unanimous/pairwise/Wilson mean exactly the same thing for humans as for the model — floor and ceiling become columns of one quantity. `labels.ordering()` / `_stratum_block()` is the second consumer of the ranking metrics: per stratum it emits average_precision (expected ties) plus ap_optimistic and ap_pessimistic, precision_at_k with both `k` and `k_requested`, positive_rate, tie_histogram, and TWO separate denominators — `label_coverage` (labelled/members) and `coverage` (Ranked.coverage(), scored/labelled). `gate_rejected` is REFUSED by name rather than filtered and appears only as `recall_bound`, a count with a Wilson interval and deliberately no `rate` key.
